_note: The Day 2 (Malware) work order. Same format as day1_recovery.json. attacks: the Response patterns that got through become these repairs. Components: program (FixBlueScreen), updates (SwitchPanel), scan (ScanClean), file_server (the final check, FileServerRepair).

room.controls: WASD / arrows: move     E: use     Esc: pause
room.waiting_body: Response has not confirmed that the malware is contained. You can look around, but the equipment must stay disconnected.
room.all_done: Checks complete. Return to the office entrance to finish.
room.summary_body: The repairs and the final check passed.
room.summary_lesson: Malware is stopped by approved programs, updates and an antivirus that stays on. Keep all three in place.

comments.clean: Joshua: Every fix was right the first time. Ben can get back to work.
comments.done: Joshua: Everything is fixed. Next time, read the reason before trying again.

task_ui.hint: Take your time. Read the labels before choosing.

case.brief: The malware is stopped, but it left a mess. Ben's laptop crashes, the other laptops still have an open hole, and a spy may still be hiding. Fix each one, then check Ben can work again.
case.lesson: On your own computer: keep it updated, keep the antivirus on, and install programs only from places you trust.

program.title: Fix the blue screen
program.instruction: Ben's laptop crashes when it starts. Find out why, start it safely, and take the bad program off.
program.lesson: A crash usually follows a recent change. Safe Mode starts with only the basics, so the bad program cannot run.

screen.title: :(  Ben's laptop ran into a problem
safe_lines: Only the basic programs are running.
The bad program cannot run here.

steps.question: What does the stop code tell you?

options.label: The screen is broken.
options.reason: The screen is fine. The message comes from the system, not the monitor.

options.label: Something the system needs stopped working.
options.reason: Yes. A part the system needs stopped, so something must have changed.

options.label: Ben typed something wrong.
options.reason: A typing mistake cannot cause this. The system itself stopped.

steps.question: Which change came just before the crash?

options.label: 03:00   Windows update (every laptop)
options.reason: Every laptop got this update and only Ben's crashes. It was also hours earlier.

options.label: 14:03   UpdateHelper.exe installed (Ben's laptop)
options.reason: Right. A crash usually follows a recent change on that computer, and this one came minutes before.

options.label: 11:20   DesignPro installed (Dana's laptop)
options.reason: That is another laptop. It runs fine.

steps.question: How do you start the laptop so the bad program cannot run?

options.label: Start normally
options.reason: It would crash again. The bad program starts with Windows, so you would be stuck in a loop.

options.label: Reinstall Windows
options.reason: That would erase Ben's files. Try the gentle fix first.

options.label: Safe Mode
options.reason: Safe Mode starts with only the basics. The bad program cannot run, so you can remove it.

options.label: Ignore it
options.reason: Ben cannot work on a laptop that keeps crashing.

steps.question: Remove the program that is not on the approved list (Office Suite, Browser, PDF Reader, Backup Agent, Accounting Tool).
steps.hint: Check each program against the approved list.

items.label: Office Suite
items.reason: Approved, and Ben needs it. Keep it.

items.label: UpdateHelper.exe
items.reason: Removed. A name that sounds helpful is not proof. The approved list is.

items.label: Browser
items.reason: Approved, and Ben needs it. Keep it.

items.label: Backup Agent
items.reason: Approved. It keeps Ben's files safe. Keep it.

steps.question: The bad program is gone. What now?

options.label: Stay in Safe Mode
options.reason: Safe Mode is limited. Ben needs his normal programs, so restart normally.

options.label: Restart normally
options.reason: Restarted. The laptop starts without the crash.

program.success: The laptop starts again. The bad program is gone and Ben's files are safe.

updates.title: Update the other laptops
updates.instruction: The worm used a hole that an update would have closed. Turn updates on for every laptop that is out of date.
updates.lesson: Updates close the holes that worms use. A laptop that is already up to date needs nothing.
updates.pick: Which laptops are out of date? Turn their updates on.
updates.updated: The hole is closed on {laptop}. {left} switch(es) still off.

items.label: Ben's laptop
items.note_off: Out of date: the hole is open.

items.label: Carla's laptop
items.reason: Carla's laptop is already up to date. Leave it on.

items.label: Dana's laptop
items.note_off: Out of date: the hole is open.

items.label: Reception laptop
items.note_off: Out of date: the hole is open.

updates.success: Every laptop is up to date. The hole the worm used is closed.

scan.title: Scan and clean
scan.instruction: Spyware was hiding on Ben's laptop. Turn the protection back on, scan, then isolate only the real threats.
scan.lesson: Turn the protection back on first, then clean. Not every warning is a threat.
scan.scan_locked: The scan will not run while the antivirus is off. Turn the protection on first.
scan.protection_on: The antivirus is on. Now run the scan.
scan.scanning: Scanning... the antivirus looks at every file.
scan.found: The scan found 3 items. Not every warning is a threat. Isolate only the threats.

items.label: update_helper.dll
items.detail: Part of UpdateHelper. Calls an outside address.
items.reason: Isolated. It was the part that phoned home.

items.label: holiday_photo.jpg
items.detail: Ben's picture. Flagged because it was just opened.
items.reason: That is only Ben's photo. A warning is not always a threat. Leave it alone.

items.label: sys32.tmp
items.detail: Hidden file that writes down what Ben types.
items.reason: Isolated. The spy can no longer record anything.

scan.success: The antivirus is on and the threats are isolated. Ben's laptop is clean.

file_server.title: Back to work
file_server.instruction: Check Ben's laptop the way he uses it every day. Each check proves one repair worked.
file_server.lesson: Recovery is finished only when the person can work normally again and you have checked it.

checks.label: ORDINARY FILE
checks.expected: Trusted record: Ben's budget sheet should open.
checks.passed: The budget sheet opened and its numbers are right.
checks.failed: The budget sheet would not open. Do not mark recovery complete.

checks.label: APPROVED PROGRAM
checks.expected: Trusted record: the Office Suite should start.
checks.passed: The Office Suite started and nothing else started with it.
checks.failed: A program is not starting as it should. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: ANTIVIRUS
checks.expected: Trusted record: the antivirus should be on.
checks.passed: The antivirus is on and up to date.
checks.failed: The antivirus is still off. Recovery stays open.

file_server.all_checks: Run every check before confirming recovery.
file_server.failed: A check failed. Keep recovery open and ask the response team to address the result.
file_server.success: The file opened, the approved program started and the antivirus is on. Ben is back to work.

response_outcome.summary: Response contained the malware. Ben's laptop and the others are ready for repairs.
